method: The reflectometer launches a pulse down the cable and times the echo, which travels out to the fault and back, so the distance to the fault is half the round-trip delay multiplied by the signal speed. The signal speed is the velocity factor times the speed of light in vacuum, 299792458 m/s, and the dielectric constant of a homogeneous insulator is one over the velocity factor squared. With velocity factor vf and round-trip delay t in nanoseconds the distance is vf * c * t * 1e-9 / 2, the one-way delay is t / 2, the round-trip delay for a cable of length L is 2L / (vf * c), and when a cable length is supplied the position along the run is the distance divided by that length as a percentage. Feet are metres divided by 0.3048. Distances in metres and feet are rounded to 0.001, the one-way delay to 0.001 ns, the signal speed to the nearest m/s, the dielectric constant to 0.001 and the position to 0.1 percent. Velocity factors from 0.1 to 0.99, round-trip delays greater than 0 and at most 1000000 ns, and an optional cable length greater than 0 and at most 100000 m are accepted. Text, exponent notation, a blank velocity factor or delay, a value outside those ranges, zero or negative values and a malformed decimal are refused with the exact reason, and decimal commas are accepted. A distance beyond the supplied cable length is reported with a warning rather than refused. This is arithmetic on the numbers you measured: it does not measure the cable, does not model dispersion, a splice, a splitter or a bridged tap, and cannot tell a fault from the far end of an unmatched cable. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: A time-domain reflectometer times the echo of a pulse that travels to the discontinuity and back, so the cable distance is half the round-trip time times the signal speed in the cable.
The velocity factor of a cable is the signal speed divided by the speed of light in vacuum, about 0.66 for solid polyethylene and 0.80 to 0.88 for foam dielectric.
For a homogeneous dielectric the velocity factor is one over the square root of the relative permittivity, so the dielectric constant is the reciprocal square of the velocity factor.
